concept.name: JWT Validation Pitfalls & Hardening (RFC 8725)

relationships.description: Connects JWT Validation Pitfalls to api security oauth2 in the broader engineering catalog.

concept.tagline: Preventing catastrophic JWT signature bypasses by enforcing server-side algorithm allowlists, pinned JWKS URLs, and strict iss/aud/exp claims.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of JWT security—from alg:none and RS256-to-HS256 key confusion to kid SQL/path injection, jku SSRF, and JWKS cache-busting DoS.

spark.summary: Stateless JSON Web Tokens fail catastrophically when verifiers trust header fields (`alg`, `kid`, `jku`), skip audience/issuer checks, or confuse asymmetric public keys with HMAC secrets.
spark.keyTakeaway: Never let an untrusted token dictate how it is verified: enforce a strict server-side algorithm allowlist, pin trusted JWKS endpoints, and validate `iss`, `aud`, and `exp` on every request.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** A signed JWT (`JWS`) has three Base64URL segments: `header.payload.signature`.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts How RS256-to-HS256 Forgery Works — And How Allowlists Block It (Attacker -> Naive Verifier -> Hardened Verifier); API Gateway (Pinned JWKS Cache) -> Rate-Limited IdP -> Internal mTLS (Bearer JWT -> Envoy jwt_authn -> Pinned JWKS URL -> Internal Service).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Compare token formats across key distribution, revocation, and CPU cost. Terminate JWT validation at the API Gateway (Envoy `jwt_authn`), cache JWKS with a 60s refresh cooldown against `kid` floods, and forward verified internal claims via mTLS.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore automated certificate rotation, HTTP semantics, and API security patterns.

learningJourney.title: What Makes JWT Headers Dangerous When Trusted Blindly
learningJourney.explanation:
A signed JWT (`JWS`) has three Base64URL segments: `header.payload.signature`. Crucially, the **header is unauthenticated** until the signature is verified—yet it carries `alg` (algorithm), `kid` (key ID), and optional `jku` (JWKS URL).

Naive verifiers that obey those header hints fall victim to three classic exploits: **`alg: none`** (stripping the signature), **Key Confusion (CVE-2015-9235)** (forging an `HS256` token signed with the server's *public* RSA key), and **`jku` SSRF** (pointing the verifier to an attacker-hosted JWKS).

sectionDiagram.title: How RS256-to-HS256 Forgery Works — And How Allowlists Block It
sectionDiagram.summary: Always hardcode the expected algorithm list server-side—never read `alg` from the untrusted JWT header.

learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how What Makes JWT Headers Dangerous When Trusted Blindly works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why `kid` Injection, `jku` SSRF & Missing `aud` Checks Breach APIs
learningJourney.explanation: Even with `alg` pinned, four other pitfalls break production auth: (1) interpolating `kid` into SQL or a file path (`../../dev/null` signs with empty key), (2) missing `aud` validation lets a token minted for `service-a` be replayed against `billing-api`, (3) unencrypted JWS payloads are readable by anyone (Base64 != encryption), and (4) unknown `kid`s triggering live JWKS fetches enable **JWKS cache-busting DoS**.

ideas.title: Pin Trusted JWKS + Rate-Limit Refreshes
ideas.description: Ignore `jku`/`x5u` headers completely. Fetch keys only from your pinned IdP URL, cache for 5–15 minutes, and rate-limit unknown-`kid` refreshes (max once per 60s).

ideas.title: Validate `iss`, `aud`, `exp`, `nbf`
ideas.description: Require `iss` == your IdP, `aud` == this exact service, and `exp`/`nbf` within bounded clock skew (`<= 60s`).

learningJourney.title: Where Stateless JWTs Fit (and Where Opaque Session Tokens Win)
learningJourney.explanation: Short-lived JWTs excel for stateless microservice/gateway auth; opaque reference tokens win when instant global logout is mandatory.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: Short-Lived Service/API Auth (5–15 min)
benefits: Local `ES256`/`RS256` verification via cached JWKS eliminates per-request IdP hops.
costs: Compromised tokens stay valid until `exp` unless paired with a Redis revocation blocklist.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Long-Lived Browser Sessions Needing Instant Revocation
benefits: Opaque session IDs backed by Redis/DB revoke immediately on logout or role downgrade.
costs: Stateless JWTs cannot be revoked mid-TTL without re-introducing stateful lookups.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Sensitive PII in Unencrypted JWS
benefits: Keep payloads minimal (`sub`, `scope`, `exp`) or use JWE if confidential claims are required.
costs: Putting JWTs in URLs leaks tokens into browser history, proxy logs, and `Referer` headers.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: RFC 8725 Hardened JWT Verification in Python
learningJourney.explanation: Use an RFC 8725-compliant library (`PyJWT >= 2.8`, `nimbus-jose-jwt`, `jose`), pin `algorithms=['RS256']` or `['ES256']`, require `exp`, `iss`, and `aud`, and transmit tokens strictly in `Authorization: Bearer` headers.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```python
import jwt
from jwt import PyJWKClient

# Pinned IdP JWKS endpoint (never read jku/x5u from token) with built-in caching
JWKS_CLIENT = PyJWKClient("https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json", cache_keys=True, lifespan=600)

def verify_access_token(token: str) -> dict:
    signing_key = JWKS_CLIENT.get_signing_key_from_jwt(token)
    return jwt.decode(
        token,
        signing_key.key,
        algorithms=["ES256", "RS256"],  # Strict server-side allowlist; blocks alg=none & HS256
        audience="https://api.example.com/billing",
        issuer="https://auth.example.com/",
        options={"require": ["exp", "iss", "aud", "sub"]},
        leeway=30,
    )
```

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Asymmetric JWT (ES256) vs. Symmetric (HS256) vs. Opaque Tokens
learningJourney.explanation: Compare token formats across key distribution, revocation, and CPU cost.

benefits: Resource servers only hold public keys; a compromised API pod cannot mint tokens.
costs: ~10x slower signature math than `HS256` (still <100 µs on modern CPUs; `ES256` is faster & smaller than `RS256`).

benefits: Fastest signing/verification; requires >=256 bits of CSPRNG secret entropy.
costs: Every verifier shares the signing secret, expanding blast radius if one service is breached.

benefits: Instant global revocation and zero payload exposure to browsers.
costs: Adds a Redis/auth-store network lookup on every API request.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production Auth: Edge Gateway JWKS Cache + Short-Lived Claims
learningJourney.explanation: Terminate JWT validation at the API Gateway (Envoy `jwt_authn`), cache JWKS with a 60s refresh cooldown against `kid` floods, and forward verified internal claims via mTLS.

sectionDiagram.title: API Gateway (Pinned JWKS Cache) -> Rate-Limited IdP -> Internal mTLS

cards.label: No Header Trust
cards.detail: Gateway ignores jku/x5u and rejects any alg outside [ES256, RS256].

cards.label: kid DoS Shield
cards.detail: Unknown kid triggers at most 1 JWKS refresh per 60s, blocking cache-busting floods.

cards.label: Strict Scoping
cards.detail: aud claim binds each token to its intended target service.

sectionDiagram.summary: Centralizing RFC 8725 validation at the gateway with a rate-limited JWKS cache eliminates per-service auth bugs.

knowledgeCheck.question: An API verifies JWTs using `jwt.decode(token, public_key)` without specifying an explicit `algorithms` allowlist. How can an attacker forge an admin token?

options.text: Set `alg: 'HS256'` in the JWT header and sign the forged admin payload using the server's publicly known RSA `public_key` as the HMAC secret
options.feedback: Correct: this is the classic RS256-to-HS256 Key Confusion attack (CVE-2015-9235).
JWS verification expects a signature, not JWE encryption.

options.text: Send the token in a query parameter instead of a header
options.feedback: Transport location does not alter signature verification.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
